transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Park (CTO, NexaHealth), Maya Chen (Head of Data), Alex Rivera (Infra), Lena Ortiz (PM)
Recording: yes

Summary section (auto):
- Quick onboarding check: VPC peering pending, bastion IPs needed
- Security: SOC2 to be shared, KMS integration discussed, SSO/SAML stub config in progress
- Perf: Redwood to run E2E benchmarks and explore quantized model for cost savings
- Next steps: share docs, run benchmarks, schedule quantization deep-dive

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we got most folks, um, quick intro - Jordan from Redwood, Priya from our SE team.
[00:08] Sam Park: Hey all, Sam here, running slightly behind but good to be on.
[00:12] Priya Raman: Hi Sam, Hi Maya, Alex, Lena. We'll keep this to 45, want to cover access, perf plan, and any blockers.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We have a quick update from infra before we get into perf.
[00:25] Alex Rivera: Yeah so on our side, VPC peering request is in with cloud network team, should get the peering connection established but we need the bastion host IPs from you guys so we can add the allow list. Also we have some tighter egress rules for our staging that might block artifact downloads - we may need to open a specific URL for model weights or container pulls.
[00:43] Jordan Lee: Okay noted, I'll get the bastion IPs to you right after. Regarding the artifact downloads - Redwood typically publishes container/images to our private repo, we can provide a signed URL or a temp S3 access to pull images. There's also an option to use our Dedicated bundle so you don't need to pull large images at runtime.
[01:05] Alex Rivera: Signed URL would be easiest. Also quick Q: for KMS, do you support customer-managed keys or only Redwood-managed keys? Our security team prefers CMKs in our account.
[01:16] Priya Raman: Yes, we support KMS integration for Private deployments - customer-managed keys via our KMS connector. There might be a short setup step to hand over a role for key usage. For hosted POC we typically use Redwood-managed, but for dedicated/private we can plug into your KMS/HSM.
[01:31] Maya Chen: Great. On the SSO side, we're still finishing SAML assertions - looks like a mismatch on the NameID format with your test SAML. Lena, can you confirm?
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: Yep we saw the assertion error in test IdP; we'll share logs.
[01:44] Jordan Lee: Okay we'll get our SSO engineer to look - may be a small claim mapping.
[01:48] Sam Park: The other thing is acceptance criteria: from product we want p50 < 120ms for short chat flows and p95 < 500ms for typical user queries. Also we want cost guidance - roughly estimate per-10k requests across different configs.
[02:03] Priya Raman: Noted. For p50/p95 numbers, we need to confirm sequence length distribution and model choice. For small chat use cases it's often a 2k-context model but with short prompts, we'd probably recommend a 2k or 4k variant. We'll run the E2E with sample prompts.
[02:19] Alex Rivera: Quick question - do you do KV cache warm-up across sessions or is that a per-request cold start? We expect a lot of repeated user prefixes so cache behavior matters for cost.
[02:28] Priya Raman: We have prefix/KV caching at the routing layer and the runtime supports persistent KV cache across hot sessions. For the POC we can enable prefix caching and measure hit rate, that typically reduces p50 significantly for repeat flows.
[02:43] Jordan Lee: I'll add a checkbox in the test plan to enable prefix caching and vary hit rates.
[02:48] [00:03:00] Maya Chen: On dataset - we'll provide a synthetic set of 200 sample prompts that represent common queries and another 50 edge cases. We'll upload to the shared drive.
[03:10] Priya Raman: Perfect, that will let us measure quality regressions vs cost. Also would you prefer we run quantized model variants (4-bit) to estimate cost savings? That can shave 2-4x in compute but sometimes impacts quality.
[03:24] Sam Park: We're open to quantization as long as accuracy on critical intents remains acceptable. Need to see regression numbers.
[03:31] Priya Raman: Understood. We'll include a quantization column in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:36] [00:06:00] Alex Rivera: Regarding network egress - do you need any special ports open for your agent to talk back to Redwood control plane?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: For Private deployment, we keep control plane communication minimal and over HTTPS outbound to specific endpoints. We'll provide CIDR and FQDNs to allow list. No inbound open ports required.
[03:55] Alex Rivera: Great.
[03:58] [00:08:00] Lena Ortiz: Any timeline ask from Redwood for the POC? Our internal stakeholders want a go/no-go by end of the month (12/31).
[04:07] Jordan Lee: That timeline is doable if we clear the infra blockers this week and run the benchmarks next week. Our SE schedule is tight the week of 12/13 but we can run tests from 12/10-12/16 and present results the following week.
[04:20] Priya Raman: I'll plan for active benchmarking starting 12/11, buffer to 12/15 for revisions.
[04:25] Maya Chen: Ok sounds reasonable.
[04:28] [00:12:00] Sam Park: On procurement, legal asked about data residency and retention. We want logs retained for 90 days and audit logs pushed to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[04:39] Jordan Lee: Yes, audit logs and trace exports can be configured to push to your SIEM - we have connectors for Splunk/Datadog/Elastic. Retention windows are configurable for Dedicated/private. For hosted we can offer a configurable retention tier; details will be in the security pack I'll send.
[04:55] Sam Park: And regarding compliance, do you have SOC2 Type II?
[04:58] Jordan Lee: Yes, SOC2 Type II - I'll attach the attestation.
[05:02] [00:16:00] Priya Raman: Back to perf test design: our plan will be three passes - 1) cold start baseline (no KV cache), 2) warm KV cache with typical prefix hit rate (we'll simulate 40-60% hits), 3) quantized variant at same load. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. Any other metrics you'd like?
[05:24] Maya Chen: Please include end-to-end latency from our app edge (we'll provide a test harness), and also token-level cost breakdown if possible.
[05:32] Priya Raman: Will do, token-level cost + per-request breakdown included in the spreadsheet.
[05:36] [00:20:00] Alex Rivera: For the test harness, we'll spin up a small k8s job in our staging that hits your endpoint. We'll need guidance on client connection settings, concurrency, and any TLS config.
[05:46] Jordan Lee: We'll share a test-runbook and a k6 script example - link in the notes. Also temps for certs if needed.
[05:54] [00:24:00] Lena Ortiz: Quick question on roles and RBAC - we want to limit who can access model rollouts and pricing info. Does Redwood provide role scoping?
[06:02] Priya Raman: Yes, RBAC with role templates; we can set read-only viewers for analytics and a rollout-admin for canary releases. We'll include recommended roles for NexaHealth pilot.
[06:12] [00:28:00] Sam Park: Any risks we should note?
[06:15] Jordan Lee: The usual ones - egress rules causing failed pulls, SAML mapping causing login delays, and quantization causing small quality regressions. We'll mitigate by providing signed URLs, working with your IdP engineer, and running quantization A/B tests.
[06:30] [00:32:00] Maya Chen: One minor note, our legal team asked about indemnity and data processing terms; we can share the redlines after you send the DPA.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: We'll get the DPA and standard terms to your legal; include a link to the contract repo.
[06:43] [00:36:00] Priya Raman: Alright I'm going to summarize the perf test matrix live - columns: scenario, model variant, quantization, concurrency, sample size, metrics captured. (typing) For scenario A: short chat, model = rwd-2k-chat-v1, quantization = none, concurrency 50, sample size 1k, metrics = p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util. For scenario B: warm cache, same model, quantization=none, concurrency 100, sample 1k. Scenario C: quantized model rwd-2k-chat-q4, same concurrency, sample 1k.
[07:25] Alex Rivera: That helps. Will the SE be able to access our staging endpoint for edge-to-edge latency?
[07:30] Priya Raman: Yes, with bastion IPs and test credentials we can run from within your VPC or from our measurement agents. We'll prefer in-VPC for the most accurate numbers.
[07:39] [00:40:00] Jordan Lee: Ok closing the loop - action items we've captured: I'll send SOC2 and network diagram; Priya to run benchmarks 12/11-12/15 and upload results; Alex to provide peering and bastion details; Maya provide datasets and acceptance criteria; Lena coordinate stakeholder review.
[07:58] Sam Park: Thanks everyone - if the perf numbers look good we'll move to a short Dedicated trial.
[08:04] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll aim to have pricing for a Dedicated trial in the next 48 hours.
[08:10] Lena Ortiz: I'll book the quantization deep-dive for 12/14 and confirm time.
[08:15] Jordan Lee: Perfect, thanks all.
[08:18] (meeting ends)
